correctness.rationale: Tag two ordered draws in (X_i)_2. The 1/p_i factor changes the resulting diagonal-event weight from p_i² to p_i. Subtract the independent-pair expectation to obtain the midpoint Jensen gap for the pair of histograms Z+2e_I and Z+2e_J, with Z accounting for the other N−2 draws. Its expectation is nonnegative and is strictly positive for strictly convex f, since Pr(I≠J)>0. At a uniform edge with q=1/n, labels with signed jumps +1 and −1 produce gap 2 at s=0 and gap 1 at s=±1, weighted by 2q². Zero versus ±1 jumps add 2q(1−2q) only at each corresponding |s|=1. This gives the claimed 4q² and 2q(1−q), with zero gap for |s|≥2. The uniform Pearson affine relation gives the factor N−1 and exchangeability gives the factor W. For n≥3 both relevant walk masses have the same aperiodic local CLT equivalent; for n=2 exactly one site contributes at each parity and its mass is twice the span-one equivalent, compensated by coefficient 1/2. This verifies positivity, the doubled edge at n=2, and both stated limits with their normalizations.
residual_risks: The graph formula uses edges between distinct bins. The exact nonuniform statement is for U_p, not ordinary Pearson; the limits require fixed n. No general association or testing-power claim follows.

value.rationale: The exact cross-moment quantifies shared null variation of an order-sensitive roughness statistic and an order-insensitive goodness-of-fit statistic. It gives both a finite normalization for any graph and the precise fixed-bin limit, where simply applying an aperiodic limit to n=2 would give wrong individual masses. The all-convex coupling supplies a structural explanation for the dependence while cleanly distinguishing the weighted collision score from nonuniform Pearson.
residual_risks: No demonstrated improvement in testing power or characterization of the full joint law.
